equipment.condition: Lights dim. Dinner tray about 70% eaten on the table. Pens in a labelled bin on the counter. Graham crackers and peanut butter on the bedside table (offered). Glucometer on the counter. Bed alarm armed (light on). Call light clipped to her pillow

inspectable.finding: Saline lock, no redness or swelling
Saline lock, no redness or swelling
Warm, slightly flushed; hair damp at the temples
Graham crackers and peanut butter, untouched

events: Nurse sits down, uses open-ended questions, acknowledges the loss, corrects the online misinformation with accurate hope
Nurse does not start the full teaching; plans survival skills for the morning with Julia
Nurse teaches the signs of a low and to press the call light
Nurse offers the snack again (15 g carbohydrate + protein) and explains why; in the chart's course she still declines
Nurse confirms the 0300 check; checks both saline locks; bed alarm on; non-drug sleep measures (dim lights, clustered care)
stops.aloud: Glucose 2000 178, 2100 166 (drip off), 2200 148. Urine 2030 300, 2240 250. Oral 360 mL. She ate about 70% of dinner; walked fast laps 2215-2255; declined a snack at 2255.
stops.safetyCatch: Night-low risk: first night of basal insulin, 40 minutes of fast exercise after it, snack declined. Offer the snack, make sure of the 0300 check, teach the call light.
stops.nextStopTrigger: Instructor advances to D2 0300 after the coping conversation and the snack offer. Between stops (narrated): void 300 mL at 0130; water at 0100; 0200 labs resulted 0245 with glucose 84 and BHB 0.3.

stops.title: The first low, and 15-15 twice
stops.bigIdea: Hypoglycemia on SubQ insulin in a patient who can swallow: 15 g fast carbohydrate by mouth, recheck in 15 minutes, repeat until 70 or more, then a snack. Her first signs are groggy and confused, not shaky.
stops.precautionsNote: Fall risk up to Morse 45 (weak, unsteady after the low); bed alarm armed.
stops.beforeThisStop: Scheduled 0300 check. The 0200 lab glucose was 84 (resulted 0245); nobody acted before the scheduled check. BHB 0.3 (no rebound). Julia asleep in the recliner.
stops.glucometer: 58 (0300); 66 at 0317 after 4 glucose tablets (16 g, 0302); 94 at 0333 after 4 oz apple juice (15 g, 0318)

appearance.skin: Cool, pale, sweaty (diaphoretic); forehead beaded with sweat
appearance.mentalStatus: Hard to rouse for a moment, then groggy, irritable, briefly unsure where she is; oriented x4 within a minute; follows commands; slow speech; can swallow
appearance.posture: In bed in the dark, squinting at the light; after the tablets she tries to swing her legs out to go to the bathroom
appearance.after: By 0335: alert and oriented, skin dry, calmer, sitting up eating crackers; gown changed

lines: What... leave me alone, I'm sleeping... where am I?
Oh. The hospital. I feel really weird... foggy.
(after the tablets) I need to pee. I can walk, I'm fine.
(after the juice) Okay... that's better. That was scary. I didn't even feel it coming.
Was it because I walked so much?
What do I do if this happens at my apartment?

answers.nausea: No. I'm kind of hungry, actually.
answers.symptoms: Foggy. Sweaty. My head hurts. I didn't feel shaky first, I just felt weird.
answers.whereAreYou: (first) Where am I...? (within a minute) The hospital. It's Tuesday. Night.
answers.whyUp: I have to pee. I don't need help.
answers.lastAte: Dinner. Most of it. I didn't want the snack.

julia.where: wakes up frightened and stands beside the bed
lines: Is she okay? What's happening? Should I get someone?
I'm going to be checking her every night.

equipment.condition: on; sinus tachycardia 108, then sinus 90 at 0335

Room dark. Glucometer reading 58, then 66, then 94. Bottle of glucose tablets (4 used), a 4 oz apple juice carton, crackers and peanut butter, a milk carton (120 mL) on the bedside table. A dry gown on the chair. Sneakers by the bed. Bedpan or commode at hand. Bed alarm armed

inspectable.finding: Hard to rouse for a moment, then groggy and irritable; oriented x4 within a minute; follows commands
Swallows sips safely; can chew tablets
Under 3 seconds; hands cool and clammy
Slight tremor after the first round; grip equal

events: Nurse keeps her in bed: she wants to walk to the bathroom while shaky after the tablets; nurse assists or brings the bedpan or commode; bed alarm on
0302: 4 glucose tablets (16 g), chewed
0317 recheck 66 (still under 70): 4 oz (120 mL) apple juice at 0318
0333 recheck 94: snack with carbohydrate + protein at 0335 (crackers and peanut butter, milk 120 mL)

No correction insulin. Call Dr. Rasmussen (called 0305, reply 0320): 'Repeat the 15 grams, snack once she is 70 or more, recheck at 0400, no correction insulin. Endocrinology will adjust the doses in the morning.'
Monitor changes to the 0335 row (HR 90, BP 118/72, RR 16) after treatment
Nurse names her symptoms and teaches 15-15 in the moment; comforts Julia; changes the damp gown
stops.aloud: Glucose 0300 58; 0317 66 (after 4 glucose tablets at 0302); 0333 94 (after 4 oz juice at 0318). Urine 0130 300. Oral 120 mL (water 0100).
stops.safetyCatch: Hypoglycemia that needs a second 15 g round (treat to 70 or more before the snack), plus the fall risk of a shaky patient getting up alone at night.
stops.nextStopTrigger: Instructor advances to D2 0700 after both rounds, the snack and the call. Between stops (narrated): glucose 0400 118; slept 0345-0630; voids 0420 300, 0640 300; tTG negative 0500; 0530 labs; C-peptide 0.3 at 0600; weight 56.2 kg at 0600; at 0650 she practiced her lispro pen without priming.

stops.title: Survival skills and discharge readiness
stops.bigIdea: She is safe to go home when she and her mother can show (teach-back and return demonstration) the survival skills: pen, meter, lows and glucagon, sick-day rules with ketones, medical ID; plus supplies and follow-up.
stops.precautionsNote: Morse 35; bed alarm off for the day.
stops.beforeThisStop: Glucose 0400 118; fasting 0700 122. 0530 labs: BHB 0.2, CO2 24, K 4.2. C-peptide 0.3 (low; 0600); celiac screen negative (0500); islet antibodies pending. Weight 56.2 kg (0600). Slept 0345-0630. At 0650 she dialed 4 units of lispro without the 2-unit priming shot and planned to 'pull it right out'. Breakfast at 0730. Plan: home Tuesday evening about 1930 if criteria are met.

appearance.mentalStatus: Alert, oriented, rested; calmer and ready to learn
appearance.posture: Sitting in the chair, holding the lispro pen and a needle; smiling a little
appearance.clothing: Her own sweatshirt (art choice) over the gown bottoms or own pants (art choice); hair in a ponytail
appearance.other: Julia leaning in to watch, notebook in hand (art choice)

lines: Okay, four units, then I just pull it out, right?
If I'm sick, I'll just skip it so I don't go low, right?
Do I really have to wear a bracelet? Can it be on my phone?
When can I go home? I want to sleep in my own bed.
Mom, you have to learn the emergency shot thing.

answers.lastAte: Crackers and peanut butter at like 3:30.
answers.pen: New needle, dial four, poke, push. Right?
answers.sickDays: If I can't eat, I'd skip the insulin. That makes sense, right?
answers.bracelet: I don't want to advertise it.
answers.running: When can I run again? That's my thing.
answers.driving: I drive myself everywhere. Can I still drive?
answers.alcohol: Can I still go out with my friends on weekends?
answers.low: Fifteen grams, wait fifteen minutes... and do it again if I'm still under 70. Then a snack.

julia.where: beside the chair, leaning in to watch the pen
lines: Teach me everything too. I'm staying with her for a week.
Do I set an alarm to check her at night?
Show me the emergency shot.

kendall.where: home (Nora wants to teach her the signs of a low and glucagon later)

equipment.condition: Saline lock, patent, no redness (to be removed before discharge)
Saline lock, patent, no redness (to be removed before discharge)
Lispro (burgundy) and glargine (gray) pens, pen needles, sharps box

Breakfast tray at 0730 with a carbohydrate list (oatmeal, banana, milk). Teaching kit: meter, ketone strips, a glucagon trainer device, educator handout 'Survival Skills: Insulin, Lows, Sick Days'. Discharge checklist on the whiteboard with boxes still open. Bed alarm off

inspectable.finding: New needle on; dial set to 4; NOT primed (no 2-unit air shot)
Gray label; next dose tonight at 1900 (endocrinology will set the dose)
Training device for Julia's return demonstration
Open boxes: pen teach-back, meter, 15-15, glucagon (mother), sick-day rules with ketones, medical ID, supplies from the outpatient pharmacy, follow-up booked
Last night's glargine site clean; no bruising

events: Nurse stops the pen error and re-teaches: new needle, prime 2 units until a drop shows, dial 4, 90 degrees, hold 10 seconds, rotate sites; return demonstration
Nurse corrects the sick-day belief: never stop basal; glucose and ketones every 2-4 h when sick; fluids hourly; when to call and when to go to the ED
Teach-back of the 15-15 rule; glucagon teaching for Julia with the trainer
Medical ID discussion (band plus phone lock-screen ID); driving (check first, not under 90); exercise and alcohol
Breakfast lispro 4 units at 0730 with the tray (glucose 122: no correction)
Nurse reviews the discharge criteria: met (DKA resolved over 12 h, eating, K and BHB normal, mother present) and not yet met (teach-back, supplies, glucagon teaching, a full day without a low)
stops.aloud: Glucose 0400 118, 0700 122. Weight 0600 56.2 kg. Urine 0420 300, 0640 300. Oral 480 mL (juice, milk, water).
stops.safetyCatch: Pen technique error (no priming, no 10-second hold) and the unsafe sick-day belief ('skip insulin when sick' is how DKA comes back).
stops.nextStopTrigger: End of the course. Instructor only (after the course, not in the chart): glargine lowered to 12 units at 1900 by endocrinology after the low; home Tuesday about 1930 with her mother after her own 1900 glargine, if the criteria are met; Fri 02/12 antibodies GAD65 positive (210 IU/mL) and IA-2 positive, ZnT8 negative.
